His instructions to Zhan Tong while reading the Analects, and to his attendant officials while observing celestial phenomena and reading the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, reveal his mind that regarded all things as one body. His instructions to Zhu Shan while discussing the Book of Changes reveal his concern to order the family and rectify its beginnings. His imperial commentary on the Great Plan reveals his concern to establish the supreme standard, order human relationships, and regulate and assist the transforming work of Heaven and Earth. As for his instructions to Zeng Lu and Cai Zhe, a single principle runs throughout the entire substance and great functioning of this mind, leaving nothing out. Here we may reverently perceive his sagely virtue: lofty and luminous, broad and great, pure and refined, subtle and profound, carrying forward the tradition of refinement and single-mindedness, reverence and righteousness transmitted from several thousand years before.
Thus, in the flourishing government achieved by our august Ming, the Way is pure and the institutions complete. It emulates the greatness of Yao and Shun, taking the Xia, Shang, and Zhou as its models and implementing their precedents as circumstances require. Among its major measures are the fixing of mourning obligations for parents and lineage kin; the drawing of distinctions governing marriage among brothers and other relatives; scrupulous observance of sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples and to the many spirits; the exclusion of empresses dowager from participation in court government; and the appointment of no officials exclusively to serve the heir apparent…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
藩封不攝民事戚宦不干國典上自
朝廷下至臣庶冠婚喪祭之儀服舍器用之
制各有等差著爲條格三綱旣淪而復正
五典已斁而復敦夫是之謂治道蓋極純
而無雜矣六卿分治而無專政之嫌五府
隸軍而無專兵之患學校養士惟敎以經
書科舉取才不雜以詞賦貢賦有定額而
嚴之以擅科之條徭役有定則而申之以
私役之禁銓選有定員考課有定法而飭
===
之以專選濫舉之戒褒忠表節斥巧文言
利之徒崇儉絕奢却竹簟金鞍之獻選將
練兵而常以隹兵爲戒蠲租省賦而猶以
傷民爲憂夫是之謂治法蓋極備而無遺
矣雖然愚生所識無異管窺若夫
峻烈洪勳實未易以殫述當時文武大臣
表稱
聖德有云守帝王之心法明聖賢之道統罷黜
百氏表章六經範圍造化曲成萬物有過
punctuated:
藩封不攝民事，戚宦不干國典。上自朝廷，下至臣庶，冠婚喪祭之儀、服舍器用之制，各有等差，著爲條格。三綱旣淪而復正，五典已斁而復敦。夫是之謂治道，蓋極純而無雜矣。六卿分治而無專政之嫌，五府隸軍而無專兵之患。學校養士，惟敎以經書；科舉取才，不雜以詞賦。貢賦有定額，而嚴之以擅科之條；徭役有定則，而申之以私役之禁；銓選有定員，考課有定法，而飭之以專選濫舉之戒。褒忠表節，斥巧文言利之徒；崇儉絕奢，却竹簟金鞍之獻。選將練兵，而常以隹兵爲戒；蠲租省賦，而猶以傷民爲憂。夫是之謂治法，蓋極備而無遺矣。
雖然，愚生所識，無異管窺。若夫峻烈洪勳，實未易以殫述。當時文武大臣表稱聖德，有云：「守帝王之心法，明聖賢之道統，罷黜百氏，表章六經，範圍造化，曲成萬物，有過
translation_en:
The enfeoffed princes do not administer civil affairs, and imperial relatives and eunuchs do not interfere in the institutions of state. From the imperial court above to officials and commoners below, the rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice, and the regulations governing clothing, dwellings, implements, and utensils all observe distinctions of rank, set down in formal regulations. The Three Bonds, once fallen into decline, have been rectified anew; the Five Constant Relationships, once corrupted, have again been strengthened. This is what is meant by the Way of governance: it is utterly pure and free of admixture.
The Six Ministers divide administrative responsibilities, without suspicion of monopolizing government; the Five Chief Military Commissions have the armies under their jurisdiction, without the danger of monopolizing military power. Schools nurture scholars, teaching them only the canonical books; the civil-service examinations select talent without introducing lyric poetry and rhapsodies. Tribute and taxes have fixed quotas, reinforced by provisions against unauthorized levies. Labor service has fixed rules, reinforced by prohibitions against employing laborers for private purposes. Selection for office is governed by fixed staffing quotas, and performance evaluation by established procedures, reinforced by injunctions against arbitrary selection and indiscriminate recommendation. Loyalty is honored and steadfast integrity publicly commended, while those who manipulate legal texts and advocate profit are rejected. Frugality is exalted and extravagance eliminated; offerings of bamboo mats and gold saddles are refused. Generals are selected and troops trained, yet delight in arms [?] remains a constant warning. Land taxes are remitted and levies reduced, yet harm to the people remains a concern. This is what is meant by the methods of governance: they are wholly complete, with nothing omitted.
Nevertheless, what this humble student knows is no different from a glimpse through a narrow tube. As for the lofty achievements and immense accomplishments, they are indeed difficult to recount exhaustively. In a memorial praising the imperial virtue, the civil and military ministers of that time stated: “He preserves the teaching of the mind transmitted by the ancient emperors and kings and elucidates the succession of the Way transmitted by the sages and worthies. He rejects the hundred schools and brings the Six Classics to prominence. He sets bounds to the workings of creation and brings all things to fulfillment in their particulars. Wherever he passes …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
化存神之妙有綏來動和之應蓋諸臣見
而知之所稱允切愚生管窺之見厥有明
徵矣自唐堯虞舜以來三千餘年再覩
聖德神功之大猗與盛哉
列聖相承儀刑具在逮我
皇上峻德重光克敬克一是以
繼志述事深契
太祖之心
制禮作樂遠紹唐虞之治道純而法備未易敷
===
揚我
皇明億萬載無疆之休實于
今日再培植而恢弘之矣海宇臣民曷勝慶
幸抑明問開導諸生毋自諉曰帝王之學
與韋布不同竊意此蓋宋儒有為之言非
通論也皐陶陳謨曰允迪厥德謨明弼諧
伊尹曰惟尹躬暨湯咸有一德如其學業
不同何以謨明而弼諧何以咸有一德也
哉大學之道脩身以為家國天下之本自
punctuated:
化存神之妙，有綏來動和之應。」蓋諸臣見而知之，所稱允切，愚生管窺之見厥有明徵矣。自唐堯虞舜以來三千餘年，再覩聖德神功之大，猗與盛哉！列聖相承，儀刑具在。逮我皇上，峻德重光，克敬克一，是以繼志述事，深契太祖之心；制禮作樂，遠紹唐虞之治。道純而法備，未易敷揚。我皇明億萬載無疆之休，實于今日再培植而恢弘之矣。海宇臣民曷勝慶幸！
抑明問開導諸生，毋自諉曰：「帝王之學與韋布不同。」竊意此蓋宋儒有為之言，非通論也。皐陶陳謨曰：「允迪厥德，謨明弼諧。」伊尹曰：「惟尹躬暨湯，咸有一德。」如其學業不同，何以謨明而弼諧？何以咸有一德也哉？大學之道，脩身以為家國天下之本，自
translation_en:
…the marvel of transforming people and preserving spiritual efficacy, and the response whereby those he pacifies come to him and those he moves live in harmony.” The ministers knew these things from what they had witnessed, and their praise was truly apt. Thus even this humble student's narrow understanding has clear corroboration. More than three thousand years after Yao of Tang and Shun of Yu, we behold once again the greatness of sagely virtue and wondrous achievement. Ah, how magnificent! Successive sage emperors have inherited the throne, and their exemplary models remain fully available. Now our Emperor's lofty virtue shines forth anew; he maintains reverence and singleness of purpose. Thus, in carrying forward his predecessor's intentions and undertakings, he accords profoundly with the mind of Taizu; in establishing rites and making music, he continues the governance of Tang and Yu from the distant past. His Way is pure and his institutions complete: their glories cannot readily be fully expounded. The boundless blessings of our imperial Ming, enduring for hundreds of millions of years, are indeed being nurtured anew and enlarged today. How could the subjects throughout the realm sufficiently express their joy and good fortune!
Furthermore, your illuminating question guides us students not to excuse ourselves by saying, “The learning of emperors and kings differs from that of common scholars.” I venture to think that this was a statement made by Song Confucians for a particular purpose, rather than a universally applicable judgment. Gao Yao, setting forth his counsels, said, “Truly follow that virtue; let counsels be enlightened and assistance harmonious.” Yi Yin said, “I myself, Yin, together with Tang, both possessed a single virtue.” If their learning differed, how could their counsels be enlightened and their assistance harmonious? How could they both possess a single virtue? The Way of the Great Learning takes cultivation of the self as the foundation for the family, the state, and all under Heaven, from…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天子至於庶人一而已矣方今
堯舜在上愚生雖無由得佐下風而實竊有皐
陶伊尹之志敢因執事開導盛心而就正
焉如不以為膠膠尚當再陳未盡之蘊
第二問
易貞元
同考試官教諭湯批歷舉古人善惡可為勸
懲末復責備諸有道君子足覘子所學之大他日
必不安於小就矣
===
考試官訓導辛批評古人賢否深協輿論可錄
考試官教諭陳批條答詳盡
治莫先於任人忠邪不可以不辨人莫先
於立志取舍不可以不嚴夫忠良用者治
之本邪佞進者亂之階自昔人君鮮不好
治而惡亂好忠而惡邪然而任用忠良之
效恒少而親信邪佞之害恒多則以其辨
之不早辨耳章縫者流居常議論指摘古
今忠邪如覩黑白及至身膺厥任攻取之
punctuated:
天子至於庶人，一而已矣。方今堯舜在上，愚生雖無由得佐下風，而實竊有皐陶、伊尹之志，敢因執事開導盛心而就正焉。如不以為膠膠，尚當再陳未盡之蘊。
第二問
易貞元
同考試官教諭湯批：歷舉古人善惡，可為勸懲；末復責備諸有道君子，足覘子所學之大，他日必不安於小就矣。
考試官訓導辛批：評古人賢否，深協輿論，可錄。
考試官教諭陳批：條答詳盡。
治莫先於任人，忠邪不可以不辨；人莫先於立志，取舍不可以不嚴。夫忠良用者，治之本；邪佞進者，亂之階。自昔人君鮮不好治而惡亂，好忠而惡邪，然而任用忠良之效恒少，而親信邪佞之害恒多，則以其辨之不早辨耳。章縫者流，居常議論，指摘古今忠邪，如覩黑白；及至身膺厥任，攻取之
translation_en:
…from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, it is one and the same. Now that a Yao or Shun reigns above, though I, an unworthy student, have no means of offering even humble assistance, I privately cherish the aspirations of Gao Yao and Yi Yin. Encouraged by your generous intention to guide us, I venture to submit these views for your correction. If you do not consider them mere clamorous talk, I shall further set forth what remains unexpressed.
Second Policy Question
Yi Zhenyuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: By recounting many examples of good and evil among the ancients, you provide encouragement and admonition. At the end, you further hold gentlemen who possess the Way to the highest standards. This reveals the breadth of your learning: in the future you will surely not rest content with minor accomplishments.
Comment by Examiner Xin, Assistant Instructor: Your assessment of the worthiness or unworthiness of the ancients accords closely with general judgment. Worth accepting.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The answers to the individual points are detailed and comprehensive.
In governing, nothing takes precedence over appointing men: the loyal and the wicked must be distinguished. In personal conduct, nothing takes precedence over establishing one's resolve: choices and rejections must be strictly judged. Employing loyal and good men is the foundation of good government; advancing wicked flatterers is a step toward disorder. Since antiquity, few rulers have failed to love good government and hate disorder, to favor loyalty and abhor wickedness. Yet the benefits of employing loyal and good men have constantly been few, while the harms of trusting wicked flatterers have constantly been many. This is because they have failed to distinguish them early enough [?]. Men who wear the scholar's cap, in their everyday discussions, identify the loyal and the wicked of past and present as readily as they distinguish black from white. But when they themselves assume those responsibilities, the pursuit of conquest and acquisition [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
交誘於外而得失之念動於中則其為善
弗誠去惡弗果卒不自知其墮於不肖之
歸者亦多矣苟非立志堅剛卓然不惑其
何以定取舍之極必為君子而不為小人
也哉伏讀我
宣宗章皇帝御集歷代臣鑒三十七卷起春秋
列國以迄于元上下二千餘載自子產而
下善可為法者二百一十三人自田蚡而
下惡可為戒者七十三人蓋唐虞三代諸
===
臣已見經典者不煩重錄矣錄成
頒賜羣臣俾時觀閱思齊內省之
訓拳拳然所以
佑啟臣子者大矣錄中所載善惡之狀披閱了
然無容贅論執事欲舉其善惡之大關係
治亂安危者論別是非蓋將以觀諸生之
志頗愚何足以承之然歷觀史策忠邪治
亂之故有慨於心久矣請試陳之為明問
復人臣之善莫要於正己莫急於用賢莫
punctuated:
交誘於外，而得失之念動於中，則其為善弗誠，去惡弗果，卒不自知其墮於不肖之歸者亦多矣。苟非立志堅剛，卓然不惑，其何以定取舍之極，必為君子而不為小人也哉？

伏讀我宣宗章皇帝御集《歷代臣鑒》三十七卷，起春秋列國，以迄于元，上下二千餘載。自子產而下，善可為法者二百一十三人；自田蚡而下，惡可為戒者七十三人。蓋唐虞三代諸臣已見經典者，不煩重錄矣。錄成，頒賜羣臣，俾時觀閱。思齊內省之訓，拳拳然，所以佑啟臣子者大矣。錄中所載善惡之狀，披閱了然，無容贅論。執事欲舉其善惡之大關係治亂安危者，論別是非，蓋將以觀諸生之志。頗愚何足以承之？然歷觀史策，忠邪治亂之故，有慨於心久矣。請試陳之，為明問復。人臣之善，莫要於正己，莫急於用賢，莫
translation_en:
…competing temptations assail them from without, while thoughts of gain and loss stir within. Then they lack sincerity in doing good and resolution in rejecting evil; many ultimately fall among the unworthy without even realizing it. Unless their resolve is firm and unyielding, standing steadfast and undeluded, how can they establish an ultimate standard for acceptance and rejection, ensuring that they become gentlemen rather than petty men?

I have reverently read the thirty-seven juan of the Mirror of Ministers through the Ages (Lidai chen jian), imperially compiled by our Emperor Xuanzong Zhang. It begins with the various states of the Spring and Autumn period and extends to the Yuan, spanning more than two thousand years. From Zichan onward, it includes 213 men whose goodness may serve as a model, and from Tian Fen onward, seventy-three whose wickedness may serve as a warning. Ministers of the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and of the Three Dynasties who already appear in the classics were not recorded again. When the compilation was completed, it was bestowed upon the assembled ministers so that they might read it regularly. Its earnest admonitions to emulate the worthy and examine oneself inwardly greatly aid and enlighten those who serve the throne. The accounts of good and evil contained in the compilation become clear upon reading and require no further discussion.

You, sir, wish us to select instances of good and evil that bear greatly upon order and disorder, security and peril, and to distinguish right from wrong through discussion, presumably in order to discern the aspirations of us candidates. How could one so foolish as I [?] be equal to this task? Yet in surveying the historical records, I have long felt deeply about the causes of loyalty and depravity, order and disorder. Allow me to attempt to set these out in response to your discerning question. Among the good deeds of a minister, none is more essential than rectifying himself, none more urgent than employing the worthy, none…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
切於安民惡莫甚於殃民莫重於蔽賢莫
辱於私已持此以定忠邪之分判治亂之
幾如權衡之不可欺以重輕繩墨之不可
欺以曲直明君之所以進退百官賢臣之
所以省躬修職其要蓋不出此周召而上
名世德業載諸經典者尚矣春秋以後吾
於列國得一人焉曰鄭僑於漢得三人焉
曰蕭何鄧禹諸葛亮於唐得一人焉曰房
玄齡於宋得四人焉曰李沆韓琦范仲淹
===
司馬光傳稱子産行無越思惟義所在其
為鄭也選賢以任事立法以齊眾鄭之賢
者若馮簡子若子太叔若公孫揮若裨諶
用之各當其才民之所善從而行之其所
惡從而改之三年而有畜我田疇教我子
弟之頌使得志行乎天下豈獨鄭國大治
而已乎漢酇侯何首勸高祖養民以致賢
人曹參韓信何實進之輯和諸將除民疾
苦民安其法致有畫一之謡終身不治垣
punctuated:
切於安民。惡莫甚於殃民，莫重於蔽賢，莫辱於私已。持此以定忠邪之分，判治亂之幾，如權衡之不可欺以重輕，繩墨之不可欺以曲直。明君之所以進退百官，賢臣之所以省躬修職，其要蓋不出此。周召而上，名世德業載諸經典者尚矣。春秋以後，吾於列國得一人焉，曰鄭僑；於漢得三人焉，曰蕭何、鄧禹、諸葛亮；於唐得一人焉，曰房玄齡；於宋得四人焉，曰李沆、韓琦、范仲淹、司馬光。
傳稱子産行無越思，惟義所在。其為鄭也，選賢以任事，立法以齊眾。鄭之賢者，若馮簡子，若子太叔，若公孫揮，若裨諶，用之各當其才。民之所善，從而行之；其所惡，從而改之。三年而有「畜我田疇，教我子弟」之頌。使得志行乎天下，豈獨鄭國大治而已乎？漢酇侯何首勸高祖養民以致賢人。曹參、韓信，何實進之。輯和諸將，除民疾苦，民安其法，致有畫一之謡。終身不治垣
translation_en:
…more pressing than bringing peace to the people. Among evils, none is worse than bringing calamity upon the people, none graver than keeping worthy men from recognition, and none more disgraceful than serving one's own interests. With these standards, one can distinguish loyalty from depravity and discern the incipient signs of order and disorder, just as scales cannot be deceived about weight, nor a carpenter's marking line about straightness and crookedness. The essentials by which an enlightened ruler promotes and dismisses his officials, and worthy ministers examine themselves and attend to their duties, surely extend no further than this. From the dukes of Zhou and Shao back into antiquity, the virtues and achievements of men renowned in their age stand recorded in the classics and are exalted indeed. From the Spring and Autumn period onward, I find one such man among the various states: Qiao of Zheng; three under the Han: Xiao He, Deng Yu, and Zhuge Liang; one under the Tang: Fang Xuanling; and four under the Song: Li Hang, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Sima Guang.
The Commentary says that Zichan's actions never went beyond his deliberations, and that he followed only what was right. In governing Zheng, he selected worthy men to undertake its affairs and established laws to bring order to the people. Among Zheng's worthy men were Feng Jianzi, Zi Taishu, Gongsun Hui, and Bi Chen; he employed each in accordance with his talents. What the people approved, he put into practice; what they disliked, he reformed. After three years, they praised him in the words: “He nurtures our fields and teaches our sons and younger brothers.” Had he been able to realize his aspirations throughout the realm, would it have been only the state of Zheng that enjoyed excellent government?
Under the Han, Xiao He, Marquis of Zan, was the first to urge Gaozu to nurture the people so as to attract worthy men. It was indeed He who recommended Cao Can and Han Xin. He brought harmony among the generals and relieved the people's hardships. The people lived contentedly under his laws, giving rise to a song praising their uniformity. Throughout his life, he did not improve the walls…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
屋曰其令後世師吾之儉漢室元功舍酇
侯其誰與歸高密侯禹杖策鄴下首勸光
武延攬英雄務悅民心諸將若寇恂以下
多禹所舉皆稱其才卒成大業其篤行淳
備薄遠名勢可為後世法東漢宗臣其亦
無忝也已忠武侯亮澹泊寧靜寡欲養心
撫百姓示儀軌開誠心布公道恢復王業
惟以得人心為本境內人才如蔣琬費禕
輩隨才器使咸盡其長大功垂成而將星
===
俄殞其興漢討賊精忠大義與日月爭光
可也唐文昭公玄齡每從太宗征伐諸將
爭取金帛公獨收人物致之幕府竭節任
公不欲一物失所杜如晦與公同心輔政
公實進之貞觀之民家給人足公有力焉
史稱其持眾美效之君又謂理致太平善
歸人主為唐宗臣諒哉宋文靖公沆論治
以不用浮薄喜事之人為先節用愛人行
之惟恐弗逮四方水旱盜賊日有陳奏以
punctuated: 屋，曰：「其令後世師吾之儉。」漢室元功，舍酇侯，其誰與歸？高密侯禹杖策鄴下，首勸光武延攬英雄，務悅民心。諸將若寇恂以下，多禹所舉，皆稱其才，卒成大業。其篤行淳備，薄遠名勢，可為後世法。東漢宗臣，其亦無忝也已。忠武侯亮澹泊寧靜，寡欲養心，撫百姓，示儀軌，開誠心，布公道。恢復王業，惟以得人心為本。境內人才，如蔣琬、費禕輩，隨才器使，咸盡其長。大功垂成，而將星俄殞。其興漢討賊，精忠大義，與日月爭光，可也。唐文昭公玄齡，每從太宗征伐，諸將爭取金帛，公獨收人物，致之幕府。竭節任公，不欲一物失所。杜如晦與公同心輔政，公實進之。貞觀之民，家給人足，公有力焉。史稱其持眾美效之君，又謂理致太平，善歸人主。為唐宗臣，諒哉！宋文靖公沆論治，以不用浮薄喜事之人為先。節用愛人，行之惟恐弗逮。四方水旱盜賊，日有陳奏，以
translation_en:
…his dwelling, saying: “Let later generations take my frugality as their model.” To whom, apart from Xiao He, Marquis of Zan, should the foremost merit in founding the Han imperial house be attributed?

Deng Yu, Marquis of Gaomi, came with staff in hand to Ye and was the first to urge Emperor Guangwu to recruit outstanding men and strive to win the people’s hearts. Many of the commanders, from Kou Xun downward, were recommended by Yu. All proved equal to their abilities, and together they ultimately accomplished the great enterprise. His conduct was earnest, his integrity complete; he held fame and power lightly and kept his distance from them. He could serve as a model for later generations. He was indeed worthy of being called a great minister of the Eastern Han.

Zhuge Liang, Marquis Zhongwu, was detached from worldly gain, tranquil and composed; he nurtured his mind by limiting his desires. He cared for the common people, showed them standards of conduct, displayed sincerity, and upheld impartiality. In restoring the royal enterprise, he took winning people’s hearts as his sole foundation. Talented men within his territory, such as Jiang Wan and Fei Yi, were employed according to their abilities, and all fully exercised their strengths. His great undertaking was nearing completion when the general’s star suddenly fell. For his pure loyalty and great righteousness in reviving the Han and campaigning against the rebels, one may indeed say that he rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance.

Fang Xuanling, Duke Wenzhao of the Tang, whenever he accompanied Emperor Taizong on campaigns, saw the other commanders compete to seize gold and silk; he alone gathered talented men and brought them to the military headquarters. He devoted his utmost loyalty to public service, wishing that no being should be deprived of its proper place. Du Ruhui assisted in government with the same purpose as the duke, and it was the duke who had recommended him. That households were well provided for and individuals had enough during the Zhenguan reign owed much to his efforts. The histories praise him for bringing his many virtues to the service of his sovereign; they also say that he brought about peace through his administration while attributing the credit to the ruler. Truly, he was a great minister of the Tang!

Li Hang, Duke Wenjing of the Song, in discussing government, gave first priority to excluding frivolous men fond of stirring up affairs. He practiced economy in expenditure and care for the people, fearing only that he might fall short in carrying these principles out. Every day he submitted reports on floods, droughts, and banditry throughout the realm, in order to…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
動人主憂勤之心内行修謹不求聲譽動
遵條制人莫敢干以私宋之賢相得君以
直道終始吾必以公爲首稱忠獻公琦折
節下士急於獎拔人才嘗因歲歉賑活饑
民數百萬計兩朝定策推而弗居危疑之
際知無不爲曰人臣盡力事君死生以之
至於成敗天也豈可豫憂其不濟遂輟不
爲哉文正公仲淹儉於自奉而好施予每
感激論天下事振作士大夫之功居多先
===
天下之憂而憂後天下之樂而樂上百官
圖指斥時宰用人不公及叅知政事條陳
十事皆知人安民之急務雖不久於朝設
施未竟而規模亦宏遠矣温國公光居處
動作具有禮法平生所爲無不可對人言
英宗初立疏請信用忠直疎遠讒諂逮事
神宗極詆新法不便於民終相哲宗除民
之害急於饑渴保甲保馬市易青苗等法
力與罷除君子謂其有旋乾轉坤之功是
punctuated: 動人主憂勤之心。内行修謹，不求聲譽，動遵條制，人莫敢干以私。宋之賢相，得君以直道終始，吾必以公爲首稱。忠獻公琦折節下士，急於獎拔人才，嘗因歲歉，賑活饑民數百萬計。兩朝定策，推而弗居。危疑之際，知無不爲，曰：「人臣盡力事君，死生以之。至於成敗，天也，豈可豫憂其不濟，遂輟不爲哉？」文正公仲淹儉於自奉，而好施予，每感激論天下事，振作士大夫之功居多。「先天下之憂而憂，後天下之樂而樂。」上百官圖，指斥時宰用人不公。及叅知政事，條陳十事，皆知人安民之急務。雖不久於朝，設施未竟，而規模亦宏遠矣。温國公光居處動作，具有禮法，平生所爲，無不可對人言。英宗初立，疏請信用忠直，疎遠讒諂。逮事神宗，極詆新法不便於民。終相哲宗，除民之害，急於饑渴。保甲、保馬、市易、青苗等法，力與罷除。君子謂其有旋乾轉坤之功。是
translation_en:
…to stir the ruler’s concern and diligence. In his private conduct he was disciplined and circumspect, seeking no reputation; in every action he observed established regulations, and no one dared approach him with private requests. Among the worthy chief councilors of the Song who enjoyed their ruler’s confidence and followed the upright Way from beginning to end, I would certainly rank him first.
Han Qi, posthumously honored as Zhongxian, humbled himself to treat scholars with deference and eagerly encouraged and promoted talented men. Once, during a poor harvest, his relief efforts saved several million starving people. He helped settle the imperial succession in two reigns, yet declined the credit accorded him. In times of danger and uncertainty, he did whatever he knew ought to be done. He said: “A minister must serve his ruler with all his strength, committing himself to this in life and death. As for success or failure, that rests with Heaven. How could one worry beforehand that an undertaking might fail, and therefore abandon it?”
Fan Zhongyan, posthumously honored as Wenzheng, was frugal in providing for himself but generous in giving to others. He often spoke with deep feeling about the affairs of the realm and did much to rouse the scholar-officials to action. “Be concerned before all others under Heaven are concerned, and rejoice only after all others under Heaven rejoice.” He submitted a Chart of the Officials, directly criticizing the chief councilor of the time for partiality in appointments. When he became an Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Assistant Chief Councilor [參知政事: Assistant Chief Councilor], he set forth ten proposals, all concerning the urgent tasks of recognizing worthy men and bringing peace to the people. Although his tenure at court was brief and his measures remained unfinished, his plans were nevertheless broad and far-reaching.
Sima Guang, Duke of Wen, observed ritual propriety in his daily life and every action. Nothing he had done throughout his life could not be spoken of openly. When Yingzong first ascended the throne, he submitted a memorial requesting that the emperor trust and employ the loyal and upright and keep slanderers and flatterers at a distance. When he came to serve Shenzong, he strongly denounced the New Policies as detrimental to the people. Finally, as chief councilor under Zhezong, he sought to remove the people’s afflictions with an urgency greater than that of hunger or thirst. He worked vigorously to abolish such measures as the baojia household militia system, the baoma horse-rearing system, the Market Exchange Law, and the Green Sprouts Law. Gentlemen credited him with the achievement of turning Heaven and Earth around. These…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皆三代以後相臣之粹然傑出者也自餘
則漢有王陵張釋之汲黯第五倫楊震唐
有宋璟張九齡陸贄裴度李絳宋有富弼
王曾歐陽修趙抃包拯呂公著李綱趙鼎
諸賢皆無愧於正己然或任用不專或當
國不久是以用賢安民之志未究厥施遭
遇則然非諸賢之弗逮也至於經武定國
漢則有張良曹參周勃趙充國馮異唐則
有李靖郭子儀李晟宋則有曹彬宗澤岳
===
飛是皆豪傑之才有安民之功亦不失已
人君安不忘危如諸臣者何可少哉至於
惡可為戒如江充梁冀鳳莽敦泚輩身為
大逆自蹈赤族之誅曹操司馬懿則亦未
辟之莽敦耳皆非人類所不忍言其他如
張湯王温舒來俊臣周興為殃民之罪魁
李林甫盧杞蔡京章惇蔡卞黃潛善秦檜
賈似道為黨奸賊賢誤國殃民之元惡是
皆專私一已視國家生民之安危利病略
punctuated:
皆三代以後相臣之粹然傑出者也。自餘則漢有王陵、張釋之、汲黯、第五倫、楊震，唐有宋璟、張九齡、陸贄、裴度、李絳，宋有富弼、王曾、歐陽修、趙抃、包拯、呂公著、李綱、趙鼎，諸賢皆無愧於正己。然或任用不專，或當國不久，是以用賢安民之志未究厥施。遭遇則然，非諸賢之弗逮也。至於經武定國，漢則有張良、曹參、周勃、趙充國、馮異，唐則有李靖、郭子儀、李晟，宋則有曹彬、宗澤、岳飛，是皆豪傑之才，有安民之功，亦不失已。人君安不忘危，如諸臣者何可少哉！

至於惡可為戒，如江充、梁冀、鳳、莽、敦、泚輩，身為大逆，自蹈赤族之誅。曹操、司馬懿則亦未辟之莽、敦耳，皆非人類，所不忍言。其他如張湯、王温舒、來俊臣、周興，為殃民之罪魁；李林甫、盧杞、蔡京、章惇、蔡卞、黃潛善、秦檜、賈似道，為黨奸賊賢、誤國殃民之元惡。是皆專私一已，視國家生民之安危利病略
translation_en:
…all were outstanding chief ministers of unalloyed excellence since the Three Dynasties. Besides these, the Han had Wang Ling, Zhang Shizhi, Ji An, Diwu Lun, and Yang Zhen; the Tang had Song Jing, Zhang Jiuling, Lu Zhi, Pei Du, and Li Jiang; and the Song had Fu Bi, Wang Zeng, Ouyang Xiu, Zhao Bian, Bao Zheng, Lü Gongzhu, Li Gang, and Zhao Ding. All these worthy men were beyond reproach in rectifying themselves. Yet some were not entrusted with sole responsibility, while others did not direct affairs of state for long. Thus their aspirations to employ the worthy and bring peace to the people were never fully realized in practice. Their circumstances made it so; it was not that these worthy men fell short. As for managing military affairs and securing the state, the Han had Zhang Liang, Cao Can, Zhou Bo, Zhao Chongguo, and Feng Yi; the Tang had Li Jing, Guo Ziyi, and Li Sheng; and the Song had Cao Bin, Zong Ze, and Yue Fei. These were all men of heroic ability who rendered service in bringing peace to the people while preserving their own integrity. A ruler must not forget danger in times of peace: how could he dispense with ministers such as these?

As for those whose wickedness offers a warning, men such as Jiang Chong, Liang Ji, Wang Feng, Wang Mang, Wang Dun, and Zhu Ci committed great acts of treason and brought upon themselves the punishment of extermination of their clans. Cao Cao and Sima Yi were merely a Wang Mang and a Wang Dun who had not been put to death. All were outside the ranks of humanity; one cannot bear to speak of them. Others, such as Zhang Tang, Wang Wenshu, Lai Junchen, and Zhou Xing, were chief perpetrators of crimes that brought calamity upon the people. Li Linfu, Lu Qi, Cai Jing, Zhang Dun, Cai Bian, Huang Qianshan, Qin Hui, and Jia Sidao were archvillains who sided with the wicked, harmed the worthy, misled the state, and brought calamity upon the people. All concerned themselves exclusively with their own selfish interests; regarding the security or peril of the state and its people, their welfare or suffering, they scarcely…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
無休戚於其心其罪可勝誅耶或曰魏相
姚崇之才魏徵之直周瑜之英略趙普之
功勳許衡之學術宜皆不可泯沒如之何
曰魏相姚崇才矣而剛正不足魏徵直矣
而節義有虧趙普濟時之功渝盟之罪不
以相掩可也周瑜背漢而甘心於權賊犯
人臣之大戒餘何足觀許衡知勸元主用
漢法而不能存宋於未亡之時亦不容不
責備於賢者耳曰臣鑒皆列之善類何哉
===
曰善善長而惡惡短
帝王無外之度也仁也衆善咸備而纖惡畢除
臣子不貳之心也義也抑亦臣鑒不錄管
夷吾之例也然則人君之辨忠邪人臣之
嚴取舍將安所折衷乎曰田蚡以下七十
三人皆惡之大者人臣事君如事天斷不
爲此矧在王法之所必誅而無赦者不復
以汚人牙頰間乃若相業顯著自子產以
至於司馬光志節忠貞自王陵以至於趙
punctuated:
無休戚於其心，其罪可勝誅耶？或曰：「魏相、姚崇之才，魏徵之直，周瑜之英略，趙普之功勳，許衡之學術，宜皆不可泯沒，如之何？」曰：「魏相、姚崇才矣，而剛正不足；魏徵直矣，而節義有虧；趙普濟時之功、渝盟之罪，不以相掩可也。周瑜背漢而甘心於權賊，犯人臣之大戒，餘何足觀？許衡知勸元主用漢法，而不能存宋於未亡之時，亦不容不責備於賢者耳。」曰：「《臣鑒》皆列之善類，何哉？」

曰：「善善長而惡惡短，帝王無外之度也，仁也；衆善咸備而纖惡畢除，臣子不貳之心也，義也。抑亦《臣鑒》不錄管夷吾之例也。」然則人君之辨忠邪、人臣之嚴取舍，將安所折衷乎？曰：「田蚡以下七十三人，皆惡之大者。人臣事君如事天，斷不爲此，矧在王法之所必誅而無赦者，不復以汚人牙頰間。乃若相業顯著，自子產以至於司馬光；志節忠貞，自王陵以至於趙
translation_en:
…with no concern in their hearts for its welfare or suffering. Could their crimes ever be adequately punished? Someone asks: “The talents of Wei Xiang and Yao Chong, the forthrightness of Wei Zheng, the outstanding strategic ability of Zhou Yu, the meritorious achievements of Zhao Pu, and the learning of Xu Heng surely ought not all to be effaced. How should we treat them?” The reply is: “Wei Xiang and Yao Chong were talented, but lacked firmness and rectitude. Wei Zheng was forthright, but his integrity and righteousness were flawed. In Zhao Pu’s case, we may acknowledge both his service in meeting the needs of his age and his crime of breaking a covenant, allowing neither to obscure the other. Zhou Yu turned his back on the Han and willingly served the rebel Quan [Sun Quan], violating the greatest prohibition incumbent upon a minister. What else about him deserves consideration? Xu Heng knew to urge the Yuan ruler to adopt Han Chinese institutions, yet could not preserve the Song while it still survived. Here too, we cannot refrain from holding a worthy man to the highest standard.” The questioner asks: “Why, then, does the Mirror for Ministers (Chenjian) place all of them among the good?”

The reply is: “To give broad scope to the commendation of goodness and narrow scope to the condemnation of evil expresses the all-embracing magnanimity of an emperor: this is benevolence. To possess every virtue and eliminate even the slightest evil expresses a minister’s undivided loyalty: this is righteousness. There is also the precedent of the Mirror for Ministers omitting Guan Yiwu.” What standard, then, should rulers follow in distinguishing the loyal from the treacherous, and ministers in rigorously deciding what to embrace and reject? The reply is: “The seventy-three men beginning with Tian Fen were all supremely evil. A minister serves his ruler as he serves Heaven and must never act in this way. Moreover, their deeds necessarily incur execution under royal law, without pardon; we need not further sully our mouths by speaking of them. As for those whose achievements as chief ministers were distinguished, they range from Zichan to Sima Guang; those whose resolve and integrity were loyal and steadfast range from Wang Ling to Zhao…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
鼎經武定國自張良以至於岳飛雖其才
器不能盡同而皆忠於所事有正己用賢
安民之心人君誠得諸賢者量才授任各
盡其長而用之自足以建長治久安之業
有如魏相姚崇之依違取容魏徵趙普之
反復悖義必處之各於其所不使偽得以
亂真庶幾忠邪之辨無有遁情人臣省躬
修職亦必以是為準而其取善成身又當
充類以至其極夫人臣之義莫大於格君
===
諸臣雖賢似於此有所未盡庶幾焉者其
諸葛亮范仲淹司馬光乎必求道德明碩
繼往聖之學達先王之治者則如程顥程
頤朱熹其人而後可所不錄於臣鑒豈非
以其紹續道統無待表揚亦如皐陶伊周
已見經典不必更錄者耶程子曰為宗社
生靈長久之計惟是輔養上德朱子曰誠
以天下為己任當自格君心之非始欲格
君心當自身始皐陶伊周所以克艱厥臣
punctuated:
鼎；經武定國，自張良以至於岳飛。雖其才器不能盡同，而皆忠於所事，有正己用賢安民之心。人君誠得諸賢者，量才授任，各盡其長而用之，自足以建長治久安之業。有如魏相、姚崇之依違取容，魏徵、趙普之反復悖義，必處之各於其所，不使偽得以亂真，庶幾忠邪之辨無有遁情。人臣省躬修職，亦必以是為準，而其取善成身，又當充類以至其極。
夫人臣之義，莫大於格君。諸臣雖賢，似於此有所未盡。庶幾焉者，其諸葛亮、范仲淹、司馬光乎？必求道德明碩、繼往聖之學、達先王之治者，則如程顥、程頤、朱熹其人而後可。所不錄於臣鑒，豈非以其紹續道統，無待表揚，亦如皐陶、伊、周已見經典，不必更錄者耶？程子曰：「為宗社生靈長久之計，惟是輔養上德。」朱子曰：「誠以天下為己任，當自格君心之非始。欲格君心，當自身始。」皐陶、伊、周所以克艱厥臣
translation_en:
…Ding; in managing military affairs and securing the state, from Zhang Liang to Yue Fei. Though their talents and capacities were not all alike, they were all loyal to those they served and intent upon rectifying themselves, employing the worthy, and bringing peace to the people. If a ruler truly obtains such worthy men, assigns them responsibilities commensurate with their abilities, and employs each so that he can fully exercise his strengths, this will suffice to establish enduring good government and lasting peace. As for conduct such as Wei Xiang’s and Yao Chong’s vacillation to win favor, or Wei Zheng’s and Zhao Pu’s reversals of allegiance in violation of righteousness, each must be assigned its proper place, so that the false cannot confound the true. Only then may the distinction between loyalty and wickedness leave no true disposition concealed. Ministers, in examining themselves and fulfilling their duties, must likewise take this as their standard; in adopting what is good and perfecting themselves, they must further extend its implications to their utmost reach.
Among a minister’s moral obligations, none is greater than rectifying the ruler. Worthy though these ministers were, they seem not to have fulfilled this entirely. Were not Zhuge Liang, Fan Zhongyan, and Sima Guang those who came closest? If one insists on seeking men of enlightened and profound moral attainment, who carried on the learning of the sages of old and comprehended the government of the former kings, only men such as Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Zhu Xi will suffice. Were they omitted from the Mirror for Ministers because, as continuators of the succession of the Way, they needed no further commendation—just as Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou, already represented in the classics, needed no further entry? Master Cheng said: “To plan for the lasting welfare of the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and the people, the essential thing is to assist and nurture the sovereign’s virtue.” Master Zhu said: “If one truly takes responsibility for all under Heaven, one must begin by correcting what is wrong in the ruler’s heart. To rectify the ruler’s heart, one must begin with oneself.” The means by which Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou fulfilled the difficult duties of ministership…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其道固如此如有用我執此以往以正己
格君爲大本以用賢爲急務以安民爲實
功而於孔明興漢討賊之義希文先憂後
樂之志君實活國救民之心皆兼體而時
出之正色立朝雖使莽操京卞復生必皆
逆折不見之奸而坐寢未形之變其庶幾
昭代之純臣矣乎抑愚聞之善常隳於自賢惡
每長於自恕一念自賢百善皆遏矣一念
自恕衆惡皆生矣故必痛絕自賢自恕之
===
心而後可以盡爲臣之道其要只在責志
不識執事以爲如何
第三問
徐可相
同考試官敎諭鄧批人才之進退關世道之否泰
明于之說於時則亦難乎其爲小人矣
同考試官敎諭李批昌大之詞可知君子之所養矣
考試官訓導辛批敷陳治道有用之學也
考試官敎諭陳批以三大二難立說迥異諸作
punctuated:
其道固如此。如有用我，執此以往，以正己格君爲大本，以用賢爲急務，以安民爲實功，而於孔明興漢討賊之義、希文先憂後樂之志、君實活國救民之心，皆兼體而時出之。正色立朝，雖使莽、操、京、卞復生，必皆逆折不見之奸，而坐寢未形之變，其庶幾昭代之純臣矣乎！抑愚聞之：善常隳於自賢，惡每長於自恕。一念自賢，百善皆遏矣；一念自恕，衆惡皆生矣。故必痛絕自賢自恕之心，而後可以盡爲臣之道。其要只在責志，不識執事以爲如何？

第三問
徐可相

同考試官敎諭鄧批：「人才之進退，關世道之否泰。明于之說，於時則亦難乎其爲小人矣。」

同考試官敎諭李批：「昌大之詞，可知君子之所養矣。」

考試官訓導辛批：「敷陳治道，有用之學也。」

考試官敎諭陳批：「以三大二難立說，迥異諸作。」
translation_en:
…their way was indeed like this. If someone were to employ me, I would proceed on this basis, making rectifying myself and correcting the ruler my fundamental task, employing the worthy my urgent concern, and bringing peace to the people my substantive achievement. I would also embody Kongming’s commitment to restoring the Han and punishing rebels, Xiwen’s resolve to take worry upon himself before others and enjoy happiness after them, and Junshi’s desire to revive the state and rescue the people, putting each into practice as circumstances required. Standing in court with a stern countenance, even if Wang Mang, Cao Cao, Cai Jing, and Cai Bian returned to life, I would surely thwart their treachery before it became apparent and quell upheavals before they took shape, without having to stir. Might I then approach the ideal of an unsullied minister of this illustrious age?

Yet I have heard that goodness is often undermined by thinking oneself worthy, and evil often grows through excusing oneself. A single thought of one’s own worthiness obstructs every good; a single thought of self-excuse gives rise to every evil. Thus only after resolutely severing the impulse to esteem and excuse oneself can one fully discharge the duties of a minister. The essential point lies solely in holding one’s own resolve to account. I do not know what you, sir, think of this.

Third Policy Question
Xu Kexiang

Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: “The advancement and dismissal of talented men bear upon adversity and prosperity in the affairs of the age. If this argument is understood [?], it will indeed be difficult for petty men to act as such in these times.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “From these expansive words, one can discern what the gentleman has cultivated within himself.”

Examiner Xin, Assistant Instructor, comments: “An exposition of the way of government: this is learning of practical use.”

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “It establishes its argument through the three great principles and the two difficulties, standing far apart from the other compositions.”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天下有三大治天下者有二難何謂三大
曰大智也大公也大順也何謂二難曰任
賢勿貳也去邪勿疑也有大智而後有以
成天下之大公有大公而後有以致天下
之大順三者相因以為功者也然必任賢
勿貳去邪勿疑而後有以成天下之大智
斯二者又相待以致用者也故自其任賢
言之老成者或謂其為遲鈍忠厚者或謂
其為寡昧鯁諒者或謂其為賣直廉潔者
===
或謂其為矯激好古者或謂其為戾俗五
者之見横于中而意遂沮矣且忌者因得
以顯排而陰擠讒者因得以投間而抵隙
二者之於君心一為所乗鮮不惑矣所以
任賢以勿貳為難也自其去邪言之本姦
也而悅其有為本佞也而悅其附已本刻
削也而悅其振法本聚斂以殃民也而悅
其富國本貪汙無耻也而悅其側媚不恐
發其幽獨之私五者之情動于中而不見
punctuated:
天下有三大，治天下者有二難。何謂三大？曰：大智也，大公也，大順也。何謂二難？曰：任賢勿貳也，去邪勿疑也。有大智而後有以成天下之大公，有大公而後有以致天下之大順，三者相因以為功者也。然必任賢勿貳，去邪勿疑，而後有以成天下之大智，斯二者又相待以致用者也。

故自其任賢言之，老成者或謂其為遲鈍，忠厚者或謂其為寡昧，鯁諒者或謂其為賣直，廉潔者或謂其為矯激，好古者或謂其為戾俗。五者之見横于中，而意遂沮矣。且忌者因得以顯排而陰擠，讒者因得以投間而抵隙。二者之於君心，一為所乗，鮮不惑矣。所以任賢以勿貳為難也。

自其去邪言之，本姦也，而悅其有為；本佞也，而悅其附已；本刻削也，而悅其振法；本聚斂以殃民也，而悅其富國；本貪汙無耻也，而悅其側媚，不恐發其幽獨之私。五者之情動于中，而不見
translation_en:
There are three great qualities under Heaven, and two difficulties for those who govern it. What are the three great qualities? Great wisdom, great impartiality, and great harmony. What are the two difficulties? Employing the worthy without wavering, and removing the wicked without hesitation. Only with great wisdom can great impartiality be achieved throughout the realm; only with great impartiality can great harmony be brought about throughout the realm. These three depend upon one another for their accomplishment. Yet only by employing the worthy without wavering and removing the wicked without hesitation can the great wisdom needed to govern the realm be achieved. These two, in turn, depend upon one another to take effect.

Thus, to speak of employing the worthy: some call the mature and experienced slow-witted; some call the loyal and generous ignorant; some call the forthright and trustworthy ostentatious in their uprightness; some call the incorruptible affected and extreme; and some call those devoted to antiquity contrary to prevailing customs. When these five judgments intrude upon the ruler’s mind, his resolve is thwarted. Moreover, the jealous thereby gain opportunities to exclude such men openly and undermine them secretly, while slanderers gain opportunities to insinuate themselves and exploit openings. Once either gains purchase upon the ruler’s mind, he seldom escapes being misled. This is why employing the worthy without wavering is difficult.

To speak of removing the wicked: a man is fundamentally treacherous, yet the ruler delights in his ability to get things done; fundamentally sycophantic, yet the ruler delights in his attachment to himself; fundamentally harsh and exacting, yet the ruler delights in his vigorous enforcement of the law; fundamentally an extortioner who brings calamity upon the people, yet the ruler delights in his enrichment of the state; fundamentally corrupt and shameless, yet the ruler delights in his ingratiating attendance, without fearing that he will expose the ruler’s private secrets [?]. When these five sentiments stir within him, he fails to perceive…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其邪矣且黨同者或與曲譽而盛美賄親
者或與甘詞而營寵抑或其人能竊窺人
主意向以自結納三者之於君心一爲所
入雖有直言其邪則亦弗之信矣所以去
邪以勿疑爲難也書曰自古商人亦越我
周文王立政立事牧夫準人則克宅之克
由繹之玆乃俾乂此則任賢勿貳之謂也
又曰國則罔有立政用憸人不訓于德是
罔顯在厥世繼自今立政其勿以憸人此
===
則去邪勿疑之謂矣詩曰王國克生維周
之楨濟濟多士文王以寧蓋言周之先王
知君子爲國之楨榦也克盡二難之道故
多助于四友之臣以成其王業此周道之
所以興也又曰維彼忍心是顧是復民之
貪亂寧爲荼毒蓋言幽厲諸君不知君子
繫國之安危昧乎二難之道故信任榮夷
公輩以墜其先業此周道之所由衰也孔
子曰我觀周道幽厲傷之蓋亦有感於斯
punctuated: 其邪矣。且黨同者或與曲譽而盛美，賄親者或與甘詞而營寵，抑或其人能竊窺人主意向以自結納。三者之於君心，一爲所入，雖有直言其邪，則亦弗之信矣。所以去邪以勿疑爲難也。《書》曰：「自古商人，亦越我周文王，立政、立事、牧夫、準人，則克宅之，克由繹之，玆乃俾乂。」此則任賢勿貳之謂也。又曰：「國則罔有立政用憸人，不訓于德，是罔顯在厥世。繼自今立政，其勿以憸人。」此則去邪勿疑之謂矣。《詩》曰：「王國克生，維周之楨。濟濟多士，文王以寧。」蓋言周之先王知君子爲國之楨榦也，克盡二難之道，故多助于四友之臣，以成其王業。此周道之所以興也。又曰：「維彼忍心，是顧是復。民之貪亂，寧爲荼毒。」蓋言幽厲諸君不知君子繫國之安危，昧乎二難之道，故信任榮夷公輩，以墜其先業。此周道之所由衰也。孔子曰：「我觀周道，幽厲傷之。」蓋亦有感於斯
translation_en:
…and he fails to perceive their wickedness. Moreover, those who share their faction may offer them unwarranted praise and extravagant commendation; those whose intimates they have bribed may use honeyed words to secure favor for them; or these men themselves may secretly discern the ruler’s inclinations and thereby ingratiate themselves with him. Once any of these three influences penetrates the ruler’s mind, even if someone speaks plainly of their wickedness, he will not believe it. This is why removing the wicked without hesitation is difficult.

The Book of Documents says: “From the men of Shang in antiquity down to King Wen of our Zhou, in appointing those responsible for government, those responsible for affairs, the governors, and the officers of justice, they could place them in their proper positions and could employ and examine them; only then did they entrust them with governing.” This is what is meant by employing the worthy without wavering. It also says: “In establishing the government of a state, none should employ crafty men. Those who do not follow virtue will achieve no distinction in their age. Henceforth, in establishing government, do not employ crafty men.” This is what is meant by removing the wicked without hesitation.

The Book of Odes says: “The royal realm could bring forth men, the pillars of Zhou. Numerous were the worthy officers; through them King Wen enjoyed peace.” This means that the former kings of Zhou knew that men of virtue were the pillars and mainstays of the state. They fully mastered the way of overcoming these two difficulties, and thus received abundant assistance from the ministers known as the Four Friends, accomplishing their kingly enterprise. This is how the Way of Zhou flourished.

It also says: “Those cruel-hearted men—these are the ones he favors and repeatedly turns to. The people’s eagerness for disorder—would they willingly bring bitter suffering upon themselves?” This means that rulers such as Kings You and Li did not understand that the security or peril of the state depended on men of virtue. Ignorant of the way of overcoming these two difficulties, they trusted and employed men such as Duke Rongyi, thereby bringing down the enterprise inherited from their forebears. This is how the Way of Zhou declined. Confucius said: “I survey the Way of Zhou: You and Li injured it.” Surely he, too, was moved by this…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夫幽厲者性與小人合與君子戾宜其然
矣後世之君亦有以賢見稱而不能盡其
道者則惑之甚也噫吾嘗讀史而知其故
矣漢高帝知周昌之賢以爲御史大夫趙
堯欲竊其位不可以顯排得也乃薦昌爲
趙王相高帝信其言於是周昌去而堯得
有其位矣孝武帝知董仲舒之賢將以大
用其才公孫弘深嫉其能不可以明言斥
也乃薦舒爲膠西相武帝聽其言於是仲
===
舒行而弘得專其任矣斯二者巧中之也
唐玄宗謂李林甫妬賢嫉能可謂知其佞
矣顧寵任之益篤雖有宋璟賢相而擯棄
終身卒以成乎天寶之難宋神宗謂王安
石飾詐釣名可謂識其姦矣乃信用之獨
專雖有呂范諸賢而貶謫殆盡卒以釀夫
靖康之禍斯二者欲蔽之也賢者如此况
於不賢者乎知之者如此况於不知之者
乎此君子所以難進而小人之所以不易
punctuated:
夫幽厲者，性與小人合，與君子戾，宜其然矣。後世之君亦有以賢見稱而不能盡其道者，則惑之甚也。噫！吾嘗讀史而知其故矣。漢高帝知周昌之賢，以爲御史大夫。趙堯欲竊其位，不可以顯排得也，乃薦昌爲趙王相。高帝信其言，於是周昌去，而堯得有其位矣。孝武帝知董仲舒之賢，將以大用其才。公孫弘深嫉其能，不可以明言斥也，乃薦舒爲膠西相。武帝聽其言，於是仲舒行，而弘得專其任矣。斯二者，巧中之也。
唐玄宗謂李林甫妬賢嫉能，可謂知其佞矣。顧寵任之益篤，雖有宋璟賢相，而擯棄終身，卒以成乎天寶之難。宋神宗謂王安石飾詐釣名，可謂識其姦矣。乃信用之獨專，雖有呂范諸賢，而貶謫殆盡，卒以釀夫靖康之禍。斯二者，欲蔽之也。賢者如此，况於不賢者乎？知之者如此，况於不知之者乎？此君子所以難進，而小人之所以不易
translation_en:
As for Kings You and Li, their natures accorded with petty men and clashed with gentlemen; it was only to be expected that they acted thus. Yet among later rulers there were also those renowned for worthiness who could not fully carry out this Way: their delusion was indeed profound. Alas! Having read the histories, I have come to understand the reason. Emperor Gao of Han recognized Zhou Chang’s worthiness and appointed him Censor-in-chief. Zhao Yao wished to usurp his position but could not obtain it by openly pushing him aside, so he recommended Zhou Chang as Chancellor to the King of Zhao. Emperor Gao trusted his words; Zhou Chang departed, and Zhao Yao obtained his position. Emperor Xiaowu recognized Dong Zhongshu’s worthiness and intended to make great use of his talents. Gongsun Hong deeply envied his ability but could not openly call for his dismissal, so he recommended Dong Zhongshu as Chancellor of Jiaoxi. Emperor Wu listened to him; Zhongshu departed, and Gongsun Hong secured sole control of his office. These two rulers were caught by cunning stratagems.
Emperor Xuanzong of Tang said that Li Linfu envied the worthy and resented the able; he may therefore be said to have recognized his fawning wickedness. Yet he favored and trusted him ever more deeply. Although he had a worthy chief minister in Song Jing, he cast him aside for the rest of his life, ultimately bringing about the calamity of the Tianbao era. Emperor Shenzong of Song said that Wang Anshi cloaked deceit to angle for fame; he may therefore be said to have recognized his treachery. Yet he placed exclusive trust in him. Although there were worthy men such as Lü and Fan, almost all were demoted and banished, ultimately brewing the catastrophe of the Jingkang era. These two rulers were blinded by desire. If worthy rulers acted thus, how much more those who were unworthy? If those who recognized such men acted thus, how much more those who did not? This is why gentlemen find it difficult to advance, and why petty men are not easily …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
退也此君子之道所以易憂而小人之道
所以不易消也此大智之君所以不常有
而大公之道不易行大順之化不易成也
非君子之不幸也世道之不幸也非小人
之過也用之者之過也李德裕有正人邪
人相指之疑歐陽脩有真朋僞朋不同之
論蓋皆感時傷治長慮却顧之言也要之
邪正真僞之間本亦無難辨者朱熹有曰
凡光明正大疎暢通達無纎芥可疑者必
===
君子也回互隱伏閃倏狡獪不可方物者
必小人也張浚亦曰不私其身慨然以天
下百姓爲心此君子也謀身之計甚密而
天下百姓之利害不顧焉此小人也又曰
言之剛正不撓無所阿徇此君子也辭氣
柔佞切切然伺候人主之意於眉目顏色
之間此小人也難進易退此君子也叨冒
爵祿蔑無廉耻此小人也由二子之言以
求之則君子小人之情狀見矣然人主不
punctuated: 退也。此君子之道所以易憂，而小人之道所以不易消也。此大智之君所以不常有，而大公之道不易行，大順之化不易成也。非君子之不幸也，世道之不幸也；非小人之過也，用之者之過也。李德裕有正人邪人相指之疑，歐陽脩有真朋僞朋不同之論，蓋皆感時傷治、長慮却顧之言也。要之，邪正真僞之間，本亦無難辨者。朱熹有曰：「凡光明正大、疎暢通達、無纎芥可疑者，必君子也；回互隱伏、閃倏狡獪、不可方物者，必小人也。」張浚亦曰：「不私其身，慨然以天下百姓爲心，此君子也；謀身之計甚密，而天下百姓之利害不顧焉，此小人也。」又曰：「言之剛正不撓，無所阿徇，此君子也；辭氣柔佞，切切然伺候人主之意於眉目顏色之間，此小人也。難進易退，此君子也；叨冒爵祿，蔑無廉耻，此小人也。」由二子之言以求之，則君子小人之情狀見矣。然人主不
translation_en: …to withdraw. This is why the way of the gentleman is readily beset by anxiety [?], while the way of the petty man is not easily extinguished. This is why rulers of great wisdom are uncommon, why the way of complete impartiality is difficult to practice, and why moral transformation bringing perfect harmony is difficult to achieve. This is no mere misfortune for gentlemen; it is a misfortune for the moral order of the age. The fault lies not with petty men, but with those who employ them. Li Deyu expressed doubts about upright and wicked men accusing one another; Ouyang Xiu argued that genuine and false fellowships differ. These were all words prompted by concern for their times and grief over governance, by far-reaching reflection and consideration of the past. Ultimately, distinguishing the wicked from the upright and the genuine from the false is not inherently difficult. Zhu Xi said: “Anyone who is open, upright, magnanimous, candid, and free of the slightest cause for suspicion must be a gentleman. Anyone who is evasive and secretive, elusive and crafty, and impossible to pin down must be a petty man.” Zhang Jun also said: “One who does not pursue his own private interests, but generously takes the common people of the realm to heart, is a gentleman. One who makes meticulous plans for his own advantage while disregarding what benefits or harms the common people of the realm is a petty man.” He further said: “One whose words are firm, upright, and unyielding, without flattery or compliance, is a gentleman. One whose language and manner are ingratiating, who anxiously watches the ruler’s brows, eyes, and facial expressions to discern his wishes, is a petty man. One who is reluctant to enter office and ready to withdraw is a gentleman. One who greedily claims rank and emoluments, utterly devoid of integrity and shame, is a petty man.” If we examine men according to the words of these two masters, the dispositions and conduct of gentlemen and petty men become apparent. Yet the ruler cannot…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
能盡接天下之人亦惟先於耳目之所及
者辨之而已今夫丞弼之位皆棟輔之任
上關君德之盛衰下繫生民之休戚昔人
所謂天吏之副職者也必得有敷求哲人
之心如伊尹者可也次則願如王曾之正
色立朝者焉必得有握髮吐哺以下天下
之士如周公者可也次則願如范仲淹文
彥博之能容諫官者焉吳澄有言曰天下
之治亂在朝廷朝廷之輕重在執政論執
===
政賢否而進退之者人主之職也蓋亦有
見於此故人主之於大臣必清心以觀之
因事以驗之見其才之果可用也任之必
專不以其咈己而二三其心使讒佞得有
可乘之隙知其人之果不良也去之必决
不以其順己而懷狐疑之志俾藤蘿得有
可附之端夫然後人主得其職矣人主得
其職夫然後公卿得其人矣公卿得其人
天下固以類應之矣自古至治之世不能
punctuated: 能盡接天下之人，亦惟先於耳目之所及者辨之而已。今夫丞弼之位，皆棟輔之任，上關君德之盛衰，下繫生民之休戚，昔人所謂天吏之副職者也。必得有敷求哲人之心如伊尹者可也，次則願如王曾之正色立朝者焉；必得有握髮吐哺以下天下之士如周公者可也，次則願如范仲淹、文彥博之能容諫官者焉。吳澄有言曰：「天下之治亂在朝廷，朝廷之輕重在執政，論執政賢否而進退之者，人主之職也。」蓋亦有見於此。故人主之於大臣，必清心以觀之，因事以驗之。見其才之果可用也，任之必專，不以其咈己而二三其心，使讒佞得有可乘之隙；知其人之果不良也，去之必决，不以其順己而懷狐疑之志，俾藤蘿得有可附之端。夫然後人主得其職矣，人主得其職，夫然後公卿得其人矣。公卿得其人，天下固以類應之矣。自古至治之世，不能
translation_en: …personally meet everyone under Heaven; he can only begin by distinguishing among those who come within his sight and hearing. Now, the posts of chief councillors and their assistants all carry the responsibility of serving as pillars and supports: above, they bear upon the flourishing or decline of the ruler’s virtue; below, they determine the well-being or suffering of the people. These are what men of old called the deputy offices of Heaven’s officer, the sovereign. One must secure someone like Yi Yin, intent upon seeking worthy men far and wide; failing that, one would hope for someone like Wang Zeng, who stood at court with an upright bearing. One must secure someone like the Duke of Zhou, who would clutch his unbound hair or spit out his food to receive the scholars of the realm with humility; failing that, one would hope for men like Fan Zhongyan and Wen Yanbo, who could tolerate remonstrance officials. Wu Cheng said: “Whether the realm is orderly or disordered depends upon the court; whether the court carries weight depends upon those who govern. To judge whether those who govern are worthy, and accordingly to advance or dismiss them, is the ruler’s duty.” He, too, surely perceived this principle. Thus, in dealing with his high ministers, the ruler must clear his mind to observe them and test them through their conduct in affairs. When he sees that a man’s abilities are truly serviceable, he must entrust him with responsibility wholeheartedly. He must not waver merely because the man goes against his wishes, thereby giving slanderers and flatterers an opening to exploit. When he knows that a man is truly unworthy, he must dismiss him decisively. He must not harbor doubts merely because the man complies with his wishes, thereby giving clinging vines something to fasten upon. Only then does the ruler fulfill his duty. Only when the ruler fulfills his duty do the right men occupy the posts of dukes and ministers. When the right men occupy these posts, people throughout the realm will naturally respond, each according to his kind. Since antiquity, even in ages of the finest government, it has been impossible to…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
無小人難乎其爲小人如四凶之在帝舜
之時是已極敝之世未嘗無君子難乎其
爲君子如三仁之在商紂之時是已能不
難乎其爲君子則必難乎其爲小人矣如
此何憂乎君子之不進而小人之不退也
何憂乎君子之道不長而小人之道不消
也何憂乎天下後世無大智之君也何憂
乎無大公之道與大順之化也所謂天下
有三大治天下者有二難如斯而已矣執
===
事讀易於泰見君子之功而有楨榦之喻
可謂善於讀易者也夫凡陽必明凡陰必
晦易以陽爲君子陰爲小人乃剛柔淑慝
之分天下之大分也若聖人在上而使立
朝皆剛正之士陰邪不得以參乎其間斯
則謂之善於用易者矣嗚呼使天下盡爲
君子唯帝其難之雖然舉直錯諸枉能使
枉者直乃聖人之微權也抑又聞之二三
大臣人主所與分别賢否進退人材以圖
punctuated:
無小人，難乎其爲小人，如四凶之在帝舜之時是已。極敝之世，未嘗無君子，難乎其爲君子，如三仁之在商紂之時是已。能不難乎其爲君子，則必難乎其爲小人矣。如此，何憂乎君子之不進而小人之不退也？何憂乎君子之道不長而小人之道不消也？何憂乎天下後世無大智之君也？何憂乎無大公之道與大順之化也？所謂天下有三大，治天下者有二難，如斯而已矣。
執事讀《易》，於泰見君子之功，而有楨榦之喻，可謂善於讀《易》者也。夫凡陽必明，凡陰必晦。《易》以陽爲君子，陰爲小人，乃剛柔淑慝之分，天下之大分也。若聖人在上，而使立朝皆剛正之士，陰邪不得以參乎其間，斯則謂之善於用《易》者矣。嗚呼！使天下盡爲君子，唯帝其難之。雖然，舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直，乃聖人之微權也。抑又聞之，二三大臣，人主所與分别賢否、進退人材，以圖
translation_en:
…be without petty men; yet it was difficult for them to act as petty men, as exemplified by the Four Malefactors in the time of Emperor Shun. In ages of utter decline, there have always been gentlemen, yet it was difficult for them to act as gentlemen, as exemplified by the Three Worthies in the time of Zhou of Shang. If one can make it easy for gentlemen to act as gentlemen, then it will necessarily be difficult for petty men to act as petty men. In this way, why fear that gentlemen will not advance and petty men will not withdraw? Why fear that the way of gentlemen will not flourish and the way of petty men will not diminish? Why fear that the world in later generations will lack rulers of great wisdom? Why fear the absence of a way of perfect impartiality and a transforming influence that brings complete harmony? The saying that there are three great things in the world and two difficulties for those who govern it means no more than this.
You, sir, in reading the Book of Changes, discern the achievements of gentlemen in the hexagram Tai and invoke the analogy of supporting posts and beams. You may indeed be called a skilled reader of the Book of Changes. All yang is necessarily bright, and all yin necessarily dark. The Book of Changes takes yang to represent gentlemen and yin to represent petty men: this is the distinction between firmness and yielding, goodness and wickedness—the fundamental distinction in the world. If a sage occupies the throne and ensures that all who stand at court are firm and upright men, so that the sinister and wicked cannot mingle among them, he may be called skilled in applying the Book of Changes. Alas! To make everyone in the world a gentleman—even the emperor finds this difficult. Nevertheless, to raise up the upright and set them above the crooked can make the crooked upright: this is the sage’s subtle exercise of discretionary judgment. Moreover, I have heard that the few great ministers are those with whom the ruler distinguishes the worthy from the unworthy and advances or dismisses men of talent, in order to plan…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天下之事自非同德協恭和衷彼此坦然
一以國家爲念而無一毫有己之私間於
其間無以克濟也其要又在人主正其心
誠其意使之博選士大夫之聰明達理直
諒敢言忠信廉節足以有爲有守者隨其
器能寘之列位使之交脩衆職以上輔君
德下固邦本則天下之泰可長保矣易曰
雲從龍風從虎聖人作而萬物覩又曰觀
國之光利用賓于王此區區今日願進之
===
心也幸執事諒之毋曰書生志在温飽
第四問
李資深
同考試官教諭林批兵以不殺爲威刑以不用爲祥
茲聖人立法意也子能言之具有援據有裨世道矣錄之
同考試官教諭宋批以仁義行法是知聖人者
考試官訓導辛批詞嚴義正足見忠懇
考試官教諭陳批得慎重之意
知聖人立法之意而後可與論聖人之法
punctuated:
天下之事，自非同德協恭和衷，彼此坦然，一以國家爲念，而無一毫有己之私間於其間，無以克濟也。其要又在人主正其心，誠其意，使之博選士大夫之聰明達理、直諒敢言、忠信廉節、足以有爲有守者，隨其器能，寘之列位，使之交脩衆職，以上輔君德，下固邦本，則天下之泰可長保矣。《易》曰：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物覩。」又曰：「觀國之光，利用賓于王。」此區區今日願進之心也。幸執事諒之，毋曰書生志在温飽。
第四問
李資深
同考試官教諭林批：「兵以不殺爲威，刑以不用爲祥，茲聖人立法意也。子能言之，具有援據，有裨世道矣。錄之。」
同考試官教諭宋批：「以仁義行法，是知聖人者。」
考試官訓導辛批：「詞嚴義正，足見忠懇。」
考試官教諭陳批：「得慎重之意。」
知聖人立法之意，而後可與論聖人之法。
translation_en:
…the affairs of All under Heaven. Unless they share the same virtue, cooperate with reverence and concord, deal openly with one another, and think solely of the state, allowing not the slightest selfish interest to intervene, they cannot accomplish their task. The essential point further lies in the ruler’s rectifying his mind and making his intentions sincere, and having them select widely from among scholar-officials those who are intelligent and discerning, upright and trustworthy, courageous in speaking out, loyal and faithful, incorruptible and principled, and capable both of achievement and of holding firm to their convictions. They should be appointed to the various offices according to their capacities and abilities, so that together they discharge their many duties, supporting the ruler’s virtue above and securing the foundations of the state below. Then the peace of All under Heaven can long be preserved. The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and all things behold him.” It also says: “Viewing the glory of the state: it is favorable to be the king’s guest.” Such is my humble desire in presenting myself today. I hope that you will understand it and will not say that a scholar’s ambition extends only to warm clothing and a full belly.
Fourth Question
Li Zishen
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Military force finds its authority in refraining from killing, and punishments are auspicious when left unused. This is the sage’s intention in establishing laws. You have expressed it, supporting your statements with citations, and have contributed to the moral order of the age. Selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “To administer the law with benevolence and righteousness—this shows an understanding of the sage.”
Comment by Examiner Xin, Assistant Instructor: “The language is solemn and the principles correct, amply revealing loyalty and earnestness.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “It captures the spirit of caution and care.”
Only after understanding the sage’s intention in establishing laws can one discuss the sage’s laws.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有聖人用法之本而後可以行聖人之法
夫法者治之具也非聖人之得已也不得
已而後有法則其意固有在蓋不屑屑於
取必以窮法之用若謂吾有可恃之法無
故得以自逞以敵天下之欲此豈聖人立
法之意哉且方其法之未立也必先務盡
其本脩之吾身順以施之於天下使天下
皆入吾道化之中天下同安于其常吾固
亦得以常而治之至於天下不能盡如吾
===
意而吾道化有所不及無以通之則吾治
窮矣於是存意外之慮爲先事之防道不
足以自遂而法斯立焉法立可以通治之
變使吾道化不至於窮是法固治之具也
而實王道之權非離道以爲用者也若不
知立法之意欲以語乎聖人之法則將謂
兵必主於征伐刑必主於殺戮不窮其用
不已矣若不先脩其本而徒恃其法則將
日事征伐殺戮而日亦不足矣恐聖人之
punctuated:
有聖人用法之本，而後可以行聖人之法。
夫法者，治之具也，非聖人之得已也。不得已而後有法，則其意固有在，蓋不屑屑於取必以窮法之用。若謂吾有可恃之法，無故得以自逞，以敵天下之欲，此豈聖人立法之意哉？且方其法之未立也，必先務盡其本，脩之吾身，順以施之於天下，使天下皆入吾道化之中。天下同安于其常，吾固亦得以常而治之。至於天下不能盡如吾意，而吾道化有所不及，無以通之，則吾治窮矣。於是存意外之慮，爲先事之防，道不足以自遂，而法斯立焉。法立，可以通治之變，使吾道化不至於窮。是法固治之具也，而實王道之權，非離道以爲用者也。若不知立法之意，欲以語乎聖人之法，則將謂兵必主於征伐，刑必主於殺戮，不窮其用不已矣。若不先脩其本，而徒恃其法，則將日事征伐殺戮，而日亦不足矣。恐聖人之
translation_en:
Only after possessing the foundation upon which the sages applied laws can one put the sages’ laws into practice.
Laws are instruments of government, adopted by the sages only because they had no alternative. Since laws arose only from necessity, there was assuredly a purpose behind them: the sages did not fuss over securing inevitable results by exhausting every application of law. If one were to say, “I have laws on which I can rely, and may therefore indulge myself without cause, opposing the desires of all under Heaven,” could this possibly be the sages’ intention in establishing laws? Before establishing laws, one must first strive to develop their foundation fully, cultivating it in oneself and extending it naturally to all under Heaven, so that everyone comes within the moral transformation wrought by one’s Way. When all under Heaven rest secure in the regular order, one can indeed govern them by regular means. But when all under Heaven cannot wholly accord with one’s intentions, and there are places beyond the reach of one’s moral transformation, government will reach an impasse unless one has a means of overcoming this. Thus one takes thought for the unexpected and makes provision before events occur. Where the Way cannot achieve its ends unaided, laws are established. Once established, laws enable government to respond to changing circumstances, keeping the moral transformation wrought by one’s Way from reaching an impasse. Laws are therefore instruments of government, but in truth they are the expedient measures of the kingly Way, not something employed apart from the Way. If one attempts to discuss the sages’ laws without understanding their intention in establishing them, one will conclude that military force must chiefly serve conquest, and punishments must chiefly serve killing, and will not desist until their uses have been exhausted. If one fails first to cultivate their foundation and merely relies on laws, one will engage daily in conquest and killing, yet every day find these insufficient. I fear that the sages’ …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
法不如是之蹙也執事以此下詢承學知
有仁人長者之心矣愚何人斯足以與知
焉雖然竊嘗聞之自師卦旣畫而天下遂
知有兵黃帝時已有涿鹿之戰矣周立大
司馬掌九伐之灋以正邦國特其制益詳
耳非謂至此而後有兵之名也自噬嗑旣
畫而天下遂知有刑帝舜時已有四凶之
誅矣周設大司寇以五刑糾萬民蓋其義
始備耳非謂至此而後有刑之名也是故
曰眚曰伐曰壇曰削曰侵曰正曰殘曰杜
曰滅此九伐之義然必各有所主而後用
之也故馮弱犯寡則眚之賊賢害民則伐
之暴內陵外則壇之野荒民散則削之負
固不服則侵之賊殺其親則正之放弑其
君則殘之犯令陵政則杜之外內亂鳥獸
行則滅之是知兵也者乃稽實待虛之制
使天下知吾之有兵也畏而不敢干吾之
典吾固不得而强用之矣曰野曰軍曰鄕
punctuated: 法不如是之蹙也。執事以此下詢，承學知有仁人長者之心矣。愚何人斯，足以與知焉？雖然，竊嘗聞之：自師卦旣畫，而天下遂知有兵，黃帝時已有涿鹿之戰矣。周立大司馬，掌九伐之灋，以正邦國，特其制益詳耳，非謂至此而後有兵之名也。自噬嗑旣畫，而天下遂知有刑，帝舜時已有四凶之誅矣。周設大司寇，以五刑糾萬民，蓋其義始備耳，非謂至此而後有刑之名也。是故曰眚，曰伐，曰壇，曰削，曰侵，曰正，曰殘，曰杜，曰滅，此九伐之義。然必各有所主而後用之也。故馮弱犯寡則眚之，賊賢害民則伐之，暴內陵外則壇之，野荒民散則削之，負固不服則侵之，賊殺其親則正之，放弑其君則殘之，犯令陵政則杜之，外內亂、鳥獸行則滅之。是知兵也者，乃稽實待虛之制，使天下知吾之有兵也，畏而不敢干吾之典，吾固不得而强用之矣。曰野，曰軍，曰鄕……
translation_en:
…the laws of the sages are surely not so narrowly constrained. By graciously putting this question to us students, you reveal the heart of a humane and venerable man. Who am I, in my ignorance, to presume to understand such matters? Nevertheless, I have heard the following.

Once the hexagram Shi (The Army) had been drawn, the world came to know of warfare; already in the time of the Yellow Emperor there was the battle of Zhuolu. The Zhou established the office of Minister of War, charged with the regulations governing nine kinds of punitive expedition, to bring the states into order. This merely made the system more detailed; it does not mean that warfare became known only then. Once the hexagram Shihe (Biting Through) had been drawn, the world came to know of punishments; already in Emperor Shun’s time the Four Malefactors had been punished. The Zhou established the office of Minister of Justice, who used the five punishments to correct the myriad people. This merely brought their principles to completion; it does not mean that punishments became known only then.

Thus there are weakening, attacking, leveling [?], reducing, invading, rectifying, devastating, blocking, and destroying: these are the meanings of the nine kinds of punitive expedition. Yet each must have its particular grounds before it is employed. Those who overbear the weak and attack the few are to be weakened; those who injure the worthy and harm the people are to be attacked; those who are violent within their borders and domineering abroad are to be leveled [?]; those whose fields lie waste and whose people scatter are to have their territory reduced; those who rely on fortified positions and refuse submission are to be invaded; those who murder their kin are to be rectified; those who banish or murder their ruler are to be devastated; those who violate commands and defy government are to be blocked; and those who bring disorder to relations within and without and behave like birds and beasts are to be destroyed.

From this we know that military force is an institution for examining actual circumstances and awaiting contingencies [?]. It makes all under Heaven aware that we possess armed force, so that they stand in awe and dare not transgress our statutes. We certainly may not insist on employing it regardless. There are those of the countryside, those of the army, and those of the local communities…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰官曰國此五刑之目然亦必各有所因
而後施之也故野刑上功糾力軍刑上命
糾守鄉刑上德糾孝官刑上能糾職國刑
上願糾暴是知刑也者亦存體應用之義
使天下知吾之有刑也懼而不敢犯吾之
憲吾亦不得而固施之矣夫聖人立法固
所以嚴未然之防然其所恃以為治者固
自有所以為之本者在也是故於侯國則
修德以懷之所謂儆戒無虞罔失法度罔
===
遊于逸罔淫于樂毋怠毋荒者是已於吏
民則躬行以化之所謂正身以正朝廷正
朝廷以正百官正百官以正萬民者是已
懷之而猶有弗吾順者乃法所必討夫然
後九伐之灋舉焉則討乃天討征一國而
四方諸侯懼是為天子之兵不戰而屈人
者也化之而猶有弗吾率者法所必罰夫
然後五刑之法施焉則罰乃天罰戮一人
而天下之人懼是為國人殺之雖死不怨
punctuated:
曰官，曰國，此五刑之目，然亦必各有所因而後施之也。故野刑上功糾力，軍刑上命糾守，鄉刑上德糾孝，官刑上能糾職，國刑上願糾暴。是知刑也者，亦存體應用之義，使天下知吾之有刑也，懼而不敢犯吾之憲，吾亦不得而固施之矣。夫聖人立法，固所以嚴未然之防，然其所恃以為治者，固自有所以為之本者在也。是故於侯國，則修德以懷之，所謂「儆戒無虞，罔失法度，罔遊于逸，罔淫于樂，毋怠毋荒」者是已。於吏民，則躬行以化之，所謂「正身以正朝廷，正朝廷以正百官，正百官以正萬民」者是已。

懷之而猶有弗吾順者，乃法所必討。夫然後九伐之灋舉焉，則討乃天討，征一國而四方諸侯懼，是為天子之兵，不戰而屈人者也。化之而猶有弗吾率者，法所必罰。夫然後五刑之法施焉，則罰乃天罰，戮一人而天下之人懼，是為國人殺之，雖死不怨
translation_en:
…those for officials and those for states: these are the categories of the five penal codes. Yet each must likewise have its particular grounds before it is applied. Thus, the penal code for the countryside prizes achievement and scrutinizes exertion; that for the army prizes obedience to orders and scrutinizes the keeping of assigned duties; that for local communities prizes virtue and scrutinizes filial conduct; that for officials prizes ability and scrutinizes the discharge of office; and that for states prizes uprightness and restrains violence. From this we know that punishment, too, embodies the principle of preserving the underlying framework and applying it as circumstances require. Let all under Heaven know that we possess punishments, so that they are afraid and dare not violate our statutes; we, for our part, cannot insist on applying them regardless. The sages established laws precisely to guard strictly against troubles before they arose. Yet what they relied upon to govern assuredly had its own foundation. Thus, toward the states of the feudal lords, they cultivated virtue to win their allegiance. This is what is meant by: “Be vigilant even when there is no cause for anxiety; do not depart from laws and standards; do not wander into idleness or indulge excessively in pleasure; be neither remiss nor neglectful.” Toward officials and the people, they transformed them through their own exemplary conduct. This is what is meant by: “Rectify oneself in order to rectify the court; rectify the court in order to rectify the hundred officials; rectify the hundred officials in order to rectify the myriad people.”

If, after they have been won over, some still refuse to obey us, these are those whom the law requires us to chastise. Only then are the laws of the nine punitive expeditions put into effect. Such chastisement is Heaven’s chastisement: one state is attacked, and the feudal lords in all quarters are afraid. These are the arms of the Son of Heaven, which subdue others without battle. If, after they have been transformed, some still refuse to follow our lead, these are those whom the law requires us to punish. Only then are the five penal codes applied. Such punishment is Heaven’s punishment: one person is executed, and everyone under Heaven is afraid. This is what is meant by the people of the state putting him to death: though he dies, he does not resent …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
殺者也是故先王之治雖不窮兵以爲武
而海內乂安雖不嚴刑以爲威而天下大
順降及後世不脩其本而全任其法一任
其法而必窮其用強兵尚力以謀旦夕之
安峻法煩刑以期申韓之效程子所謂先
王之世以道治天下後世只以法把持天
下蓋謂此也夫仁者無敵孟子蓋嘗言之
誠以時雨之師民之應之疾於影響若征
苗弗克豈禹之仁未足以動人哉弗忍窮
===
黷退脩文德仁之至爾故七旬來格乃其
效焉聖人以順動則刑罰清而民服易傳
亦巳言之夫有至德之感民之從之譬諸
風草彼下車而泣豈禹之化未足以服民
哉聖人之心願治無窮德之盛爾雖一人
未順猶不足焉由孟子之言觀之則知仁
乃王師之要以其所不愛及其所愛者皆
非也由易傳之言觀之則知順乃祥刑之
要若威以亂政貨以奪法者皆非也故夫
punctuated:
殺者也。是故先王之治，雖不窮兵以爲武，而海內乂安；雖不嚴刑以爲威，而天下大順。降及後世，不脩其本，而全任其法；一任其法，而必窮其用。強兵尚力，以謀旦夕之安；峻法煩刑，以期申韓之效。程子所謂「先王之世，以道治天下；後世只以法把持天下」，蓋謂此也。
夫仁者無敵，孟子蓋嘗言之。誠以時雨之師，民之應之，疾於影響。若征苗弗克，豈禹之仁未足以動人哉？弗忍窮黷，退脩文德，仁之至爾。故七旬來格，乃其效焉。「聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服」，《易傳》亦巳言之。夫有至德之感，民之從之，譬諸風草。彼下車而泣，豈禹之化未足以服民哉？聖人之心，願治無窮，德之盛爾。雖一人未順，猶不足焉。
由孟子之言觀之，則知仁乃王師之要，以其所不愛及其所愛者，皆非也。由《易傳》之言觀之，則知順乃祥刑之要，若威以亂政、貨以奪法者，皆非也。故夫
translation_en:
…those who put them to death. Thus, under the former kings’ rule, all within the seas was peaceful and well governed, although they did not exhaust military force to display martial prowess; all under Heaven was obedient, although they did not make punishments harsh to inspire awe. In later ages, rulers neglected the foundation and relied entirely on laws. Once they relied exclusively on laws, they inevitably pushed their application to the utmost. They strengthened their armies and exalted force to seek security from one day to the next; they made laws severe and punishments numerous, hoping to achieve the results advocated by Shen Buhai and Han Fei. Master Cheng said, “In the age of the former kings, they governed all under Heaven through the Way; in later ages, they merely kept their grip on all under Heaven through laws.” This is surely what he meant.
Mencius indeed said that the benevolent have no enemies. Truly, when an army comes like timely rain, the people respond more swiftly than a shadow or an echo. As for the failure to subdue the Miao, could it have been that Yu’s benevolence was insufficient to move people? Unable to bear pursuing warfare to the point of exhaustion and abuse, he withdrew and cultivated civil virtue: this was benevolence at its utmost. The Miao’s coming into submission after seventy days was its result. “When the sage acts in accord with what is right, punishments become clear and the people submit”: the Commentary on the Changes has also said this. When people are moved by perfect virtue, their obedience is like grass bending before the wind. When Yu descended from his carriage and wept, could it have been that his transforming influence was insufficient to win the people’s submission? The sage’s heart desires good order without limit: this is the fullness of his virtue. If even one person has not become obedient, he still considers his achievement insufficient.
Viewed in light of Mencius’s words, benevolence is the essential principle of a king’s army; all who jeopardize what they cherish for the sake of what they do not cherish are wrong. Viewed in light of the Commentary on the Changes, acting in accord with what is right is the essential principle of beneficent punishment; all who disrupt government through coercive power or subvert the law through wealth are wrong. Thus…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
斯二者於五刑屬金言其烈也於四時爲
秋言其肅也雖則以剛爲體必宜以柔用
之剛而知柔則剛不過不過則中中則協
雖則以威爲名必宜以德將之威之以德
則威不褻不褻則震震則懾是故玄默如
漢文柔德若性成矣然匈奴桀驁則欲親
御六飛以征之朱黼稱其有仁者之勇薄
昭有罪則能確守三尺以誅之司馬光謂
其得行法之當豈沉潛有剛克之用乃如
===
===
是耶英武如唐太宗剛威似足尚矣然遼
左之役乆而無成從而悔之曰魏徵若在
不使朕有是行張蘊古殺之非罪旣而悔
之曰自今死刑仍三覆奏乃刑豈高明昧
柔克之義以至此耶嗟夫兵者凶器也以
不用爲勝所以先王耀德不觀兵必不得
已而用之如武王所謂寧爾也非敵百姓
也斯可已刑者死道也以能措爲上所以
聖王任德不任刑必不得已而用之如曾
punctuated:
斯二者，於五刑屬金，言其烈也；於四時爲秋，言其肅也。雖則以剛爲體，必宜以柔用之。剛而知柔，則剛不過；不過則中，中則協。雖則以威爲名，必宜以德將之。威之以德，則威不褻；不褻則震，震則懾。是故玄默如漢文，柔德若性成矣，然匈奴桀驁，則欲親御六飛以征之，朱黼稱其有仁者之勇；薄昭有罪，則能確守三尺以誅之，司馬光謂其得行法之當。豈沉潛有剛克之用，乃如是耶？英武如唐太宗，剛威似足尚矣，然遼左之役，乆而無成，從而悔之曰：「魏徵若在，不使朕有是行。」張蘊古殺之非罪，旣而悔之曰：「自今死刑，仍三覆奏乃刑。」豈高明昧柔克之義，以至此耶？

嗟夫！兵者，凶器也，以不用爲勝，所以先王耀德不觀兵。必不得已而用之，如武王所謂「寧爾也，非敵百姓也」，斯可已。刑者，死道也，以能措爲上，所以聖王任德不任刑。必不得已而用之，如曾
translation_en:
…these two, in relation to the five punishments, belong to metal, signifying their severity; among the four seasons, they correspond to autumn, signifying their sternness. Though firmness constitutes their substance, they must be applied with gentleness. When firmness is informed by gentleness, it does not exceed due bounds; remaining within bounds, it achieves the mean, and achieving the mean, it brings harmony. Though they are known for their awesome power, virtue must guide them. When their power is exercised through virtue, it is not debased; undebased, it inspires awe, and awe commands submission. Thus Emperor Wen of Han was profound and reserved, his gentle virtue seemingly innate. Yet when the Xiongnu grew unruly, he wished personally to drive his six-horse imperial chariot on campaign against them. Zhu Fu praised him as possessing the courage of a humane man. When Bo Zhao committed a crime, he firmly upheld the law—the statutes written on three-foot strips—and put him to death. Sima Guang judged that he had applied the law appropriately. Was this how one who was deep and reserved could employ the principle of governing through firmness? Emperor Taizong of Tang was martial and valiant, and his firmness and majesty seemed worthy of esteem. Yet his campaign in Liaozuo dragged on without success, and afterward he regretted it, saying: “Had Wei Zheng been alive, he would not have allowed me to undertake this expedition.” He executed Zhang Yungu without a crime warranting it, then regretted this and said: “Henceforth, in capital cases, the sentence must be submitted to the throne for review three times before execution.” Was it because this brilliant and high-minded ruler failed to understand the principle of governing through gentleness that matters came to this?

Alas! Weapons are instruments of ill omen; refraining from their use is best. Thus the former kings displayed their virtue rather than parading their troops. If compelled to use them as a last resort, they must act as King Wu said: “It is to bring you peace, not to make enemies of the common people.” Only then is their use acceptable. Punishment is a path to death; the highest achievement is to be able to set it aside. Thus the sage kings relied on virtue rather than punishment. If compelled to use it as a last resort, they must act as Zeng…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
子所謂如得其情則哀矜而勿喜斯可已
推而言之德者仁義之謂也所以爲教者
也周禮亦必先之以平邦國之九法而後
有九伐之正先之以掌國之五禁而後有
五刑之糾皆以仁義而行法也化以仁義
而法固名焉而已矣後世教之不立而責
人則重取必於就吾之法而後已焉此則
以法而行仁義也然猶近於先王之意其
所否者不知責人以何謂而惟法是逞斯
===
===
失之矣恭惟我
太祖高皇帝以神武定天下以文德綏太平於
茲二者尤拳拳焉慎重其用與侍臣
論夷狄之禍則曰脩武備謹邊防來則禦之去
則勿窮追焉
諭楊憲則曰民之爲惡譬如衣之積垢加以澣
濯則可以復潔威以刑戮而使民不敢犯其
爲術也淺矣嗚呼至哉
王言真萬世之龜鑑願以是爲獻不識執事者
punctuated:
子所謂「如得其情，則哀矜而勿喜」，斯可已。推而言之，德者，仁義之謂也，所以爲教者也。《周禮》亦必先之以平邦國之九法，而後有九伐之正；先之以掌國之五禁，而後有五刑之糾。皆以仁義而行法也。化以仁義，而法固名焉而已矣。後世教之不立，而責人則重，取必於就吾之法而後已焉。此則以法而行仁義也。然猶近於先王之意。其所否者，不知責人以何謂，而惟法是逞，斯失之矣。
恭惟我太祖高皇帝，以神武定天下，以文德綏太平，於茲二者尤拳拳焉，慎重其用。與侍臣論夷狄之禍，則曰：「脩武備，謹邊防，來則禦之，去則勿窮追焉。」諭楊憲則曰：「民之爲惡，譬如衣之積垢，加以澣濯，則可以復潔。威以刑戮，而使民不敢犯，其爲術也淺矣。」嗚呼，至哉！王言真萬世之龜鑑。願以是爲獻，不識執事者
translation_en:
…as Master Zeng said, “If you ascertain the facts of their case, then feel sorrow and compassion, and do not rejoice.” Only then is it acceptable. To extend the argument: virtue means benevolence and righteousness; these are the means of moral instruction. The Rites of Zhou likewise necessarily places the nine statutes for bringing peace to the states before the corrective measures of the nine punitive expeditions, and the five prohibitions governing the state before correction through the five punishments. In all these cases, law is administered through benevolence and righteousness. When people are transformed through benevolence and righteousness, law indeed remains in name alone. In later ages, moral instruction was not established, yet heavy demands were made upon people: rulers insisted on bringing them into conformity with their laws before they would rest. This amounts to implementing benevolence and righteousness through law. Yet it still approaches the intention of the former kings. Those who depart from this [?] do not understand on what grounds people should be held accountable, but merely give free rein to the law. Here they have gone astray.
I reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao settled the realm through divine martial prowess and secured peace through civil virtue. He was especially solicitous concerning these two matters—warfare and punishment—and exercised great caution in their use. Discussing the threat posed by the Yi and Di peoples with his attendant officials, he said: “Maintain military preparedness and guard the frontiers carefully. When they come, repel them; when they withdraw, do not pursue them to exhaustion.” Instructing Yang Xian, he said: “The people’s wrongdoing is like dirt accumulating on clothing: wash it, and it can become clean again. To intimidate the people with punishment and execution so that they dare not offend is a shallow method indeed.” Ah, how consummate! These royal words are truly a guide and mirror for all ages. I wish to submit this for your consideration, though I do not know whether you, the officials charged with this matter…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
然否
第五問
蔣時行
考試官訓導辛批列陳十困八危盡廣西之患而
併兵屯戍之策鑿鑿可行通達時務士也高薦允宜
考試官教諭陳批憂先鄉土以措諸天下可也
天下之所可畏者勢也所不可忽者時也
所可恃者人也所不可必者權也夫勢必
積而後成智者不俟其既著而後能知及
===
其成於既久果如昔之所料則其將來又
可知矣此則可畏之甚也失今不圖所以
處之之道將必至於極盛而不可為仁者
見之不能不惻然于懷此則時之不可失
也然隨時補救調停寬其一分使受一分
之惠其責在於有司之得人耳此特可濟
萬分之一終無救於必然之弊必大更張
布置昔之所有而今之所失者復之昔之
所無而今之所有者去之所不可去前所
punctuated:
然否？
第五問
蔣時行
考試官訓導辛批：列陳十困八危，盡廣西之患，而併兵屯戍之策，鑿鑿可行。通達時務士也，高薦允宜。
考試官教諭陳批：憂先鄉土，以措諸天下，可也。
天下之所可畏者，勢也；所不可忽者，時也；所可恃者，人也；所不可必者，權也。夫勢必積而後成，智者不俟其既著而後能知。及其成於既久，果如昔之所料，則其將來又可知矣。此則可畏之甚也。失今不圖所以處之之道，將必至於極盛而不可為。仁者見之，不能不惻然于懷，此則時之不可失也。然隨時補救調停，寬其一分，使受一分之惠，其責在於有司之得人耳。此特可濟萬分之一，終無救於必然之弊。必大更張布置，昔之所有而今之所失者復之，昔之所無而今之所有者去之。所不可去，前所
translation_en:
…whether you consider this correct?
Fifth Policy Question
Jiang Shixing
Comment by Examiner Xin, Assistant Instructor: He enumerates ten hardships and eight dangers, fully setting forth Guangxi’s troubles. His proposals for consolidating troops and stationing garrisons are demonstrably practicable. He is a scholar thoroughly conversant with current affairs; recommending him highly is entirely appropriate.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: To concern oneself first with one’s native region and then apply this concern throughout the realm is commendable.
What is to be feared in the realm is the momentum of circumstances; what must not be neglected is the opportune moment; what can be relied upon is people; what cannot be counted upon is the power to act. The momentum of circumstances takes shape only through accumulation. The wise need not wait until it becomes manifest before recognizing it. Once it has long been established, if it proves just as they formerly anticipated, its future course can also be known. This is what makes it so deeply fearsome. If we let the present opportunity slip without devising a way to address it, it will inevitably reach such strength that nothing can be done. A humane person, seeing this, cannot but feel anguish at heart. This is why the opportune moment must not be lost.
Yet to remedy and adjust matters as circumstances require, easing the burden by some measure so that the people receive a corresponding measure of benefit, depends upon securing the right people for the responsible offices. This can alleviate only one ten-thousandth of the difficulty; ultimately it cannot avert the harmful consequences that must ensue. There must be a thorough reorganization of arrangements: restore what formerly existed but has now been lost, and remove what did not formerly exist but is now present. As for what cannot be removed, what previously …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未計後將至於無計者作何術以處之此
則權在
朝廷與執政大臣非區區有司所能自盡者
也執此以論廣西乃爲今日對證之方願
毋拘以文法俾得錯綜繹其見聞之略以
悉一方之利害可乎明問有曰利民莫先
於財財者民之喉命仁人之言其利溥哉
又曰觀於廣西四者之患俱備不知在昔
何如興言及此何其幸哉夫廣西無他物
===
產惟農而已近來之農有十困焉膏腴之
田多沒賊巢困於復業之難也村落之田
防賊出沒困於耕穫之難也附郭之田戎
馬蹂踐困於防畛之難也高者不禁十日
之晴困於備旱之難也低者漂于一夜之
漲困於防潦之難也殺敗墟里荆棘封丘
困於番耕之難也避賊處所原隰亢惡困
於開墾之難也收成甫畢剽奪者至困於
蓋藏之難也掠去人口懸價待贖困於立
punctuated:
未計、後將至於無計者，作何術以處之？此則權在朝廷與執政大臣，非區區有司所能自盡者也。執此以論廣西，乃爲今日對證之方。願毋拘以文法，俾得錯綜繹其見聞之略，以悉一方之利害，可乎？明問有曰：「利民莫先於財。」財者，民之喉命。仁人之言，其利溥哉！又曰：「觀於廣西，四者之患俱備，不知在昔何如？」興言及此，何其幸哉！

夫廣西無他物產，惟農而已。近來之農，有十困焉：膏腴之田，多沒賊巢，困於復業之難也；村落之田，防賊出沒，困於耕穫之難也；附郭之田，戎馬蹂踐，困於防畛之難也；高者不禁十日之晴，困於備旱之難也；低者漂于一夜之漲，困於防潦之難也；殺敗墟里，荆棘封丘，困於番耕之難也；避賊處所，原隰亢惡，困於開墾之難也；收成甫畢，剽奪者至，困於蓋藏之難也；掠去人口，懸價待贖，困於立
translation_en:
…not planned for, and for which later there will be no possible plan—by what means should these be addressed? Authority over this rests with the court and the chief ministers; it is beyond what mere local officials can accomplish on their own. Applying this reasoning to Guangxi would provide a remedy suited to its present symptoms. Might I ask not to be constrained by formal rules, but to be allowed to draw together and explain the essentials of what I have seen and heard, so as to set forth fully what benefits and harms this region? Your discerning question states: “In benefiting the people, nothing takes precedence over material resources.” Material resources are the people's lifeline. How far-reaching are the benefits of these words from a benevolent person! It further states: “Looking at Guangxi, all four afflictions are present; we do not know how things were in the past.” How fortunate that you have raised these matters!

Guangxi has no other products; it depends solely on farming. In recent times, farming has faced ten hardships. Much fertile land has fallen into the hands of bandits and become their lairs: the hardship lies in the difficulty of resuming cultivation. In village fields, people must guard against bandits appearing and disappearing: the hardship lies in the difficulty of plowing and harvesting. Fields adjoining city walls are trampled by military horses: the hardship lies in the difficulty of protecting field boundaries. Higher ground cannot withstand ten days of clear weather: the hardship lies in the difficulty of preparing against drought. Lower ground is inundated by a single night's rising waters: the hardship lies in the difficulty of preventing flood damage. Villages have been ravaged by slaughter and destruction, and thorns cover the mounds: the hardship lies in the difficulty of turning the soil again [?]. In places where people take refuge from bandits, both uplands and lowlands are parched and poor: the hardship lies in the difficulty of opening land for cultivation. As soon as the harvest is finished, plunderers arrive: the hardship lies in the difficulty of storing it safely. People are carried off, and a price is set for their ransom: the hardship lies in the difficulty of sustaining…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣西鄉試錄
text:
命之難也乞貸於人必倍其息困於通濟
之難也凡此十者皆民之大患而十者之
外有八危焉瘴疫失耕阽於死亡其危一
也水旱無收阽於死亡其危二也賊盜妨
農阽於死亡其危三也役期漸數阽於死
亡其危四也徵科漸增阽於死亡其危五
也逋負日積阽於死亡其危六也兵革不
息阽於死亡其危七也稱貸無門阽於死
亡其危八也夫民負此十困而無一舒阽
===
於八危而無一濟其勢何如哉夫因往可
以推來即今可以知後他日何如哉聞之
國初雖有猺獞雜居于間其類尚寡故古田
懷遠皆為上縣自宣德正統以來貴州之
夷由黎平透入茲土依類附黨以生以育
動以萬計其禍遂蔓延不支二邑淪為賊
巢而賊勢大張民之失業者多矣
國初雖有官兵與民戍守其守有要故本省
衛所尚足以禦自成化以來溪峒之蠻負
punctuated:
命之難也。乞貸於人，必倍其息，困於通濟之難也。凡此十者，皆民之大患，而十者之外，有八危焉：瘴疫失耕，阽於死亡，其危一也；水旱無收，阽於死亡，其危二也；賊盜妨農，阽於死亡，其危三也；役期漸數，阽於死亡，其危四也；徵科漸增，阽於死亡，其危五也；逋負日積，阽於死亡，其危六也；兵革不息，阽於死亡，其危七也；稱貸無門，阽於死亡，其危八也。夫民負此十困而無一舒，阽於八危而無一濟，其勢何如哉？夫因往可以推來，即今可以知後，他日何如哉？
聞之，國初雖有猺獞雜居于間，其類尚寡，故古田、懷遠皆為上縣。自宣德、正統以來，貴州之夷由黎平透入茲土，依類附黨，以生以育，動以萬計，其禍遂蔓延不支。二邑淪為賊巢，而賊勢大張，民之失業者多矣。
國初雖有官兵與民戍守，其守有要，故本省衛所尚足以禦。自成化以來，溪峒之蠻負
translation_en:
…the difficulty of sustaining life. When they beg loans from others, they must pay double in interest: they suffer from the difficulty of obtaining financial relief. All these ten are grave afflictions of the people, and beyond these ten there are eight dangers. Miasmatic epidemics prevent cultivation, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the first danger. Floods and drought leave them without a harvest, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the second danger. Bandits obstruct farming, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the third danger. Periods of service become increasingly frequent, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the fourth danger. Tax assessments steadily increase, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the fifth danger. Arrears accumulate daily, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the sixth danger. Warfare never ceases, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the seventh danger. They have nowhere to borrow, bringing them to the brink of death: this is the eighth danger. When the people bear these ten hardships without relief from a single one, and stand on the brink of these eight dangers without help in any of them, what must their plight be? From the past we can infer what is to come, and from the present we can know the future. What will their plight be in days to come?
I have heard that at the founding of the dynasty, although Yao and Zhuang lived interspersed among the inhabitants, their numbers were still small. Thus Gutian and Huaiyuan were both upper-grade counties.
